issues.description: `build_msd_circ`'s second returned list is documented inconsistently. The problem statement says it must be the measurement indices for the destructive X-basis measurements of the 15 tetrahedral-code qubits (used for error detection). The template docstring instead describes the second list as indices of the 'final X-basis measurements of the distilled state', which is a different qubit/measurement and will cause students to index the wrong measurement results in later steps.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template docstring for `build_msd_circ` so the second return value is described as: 'indices of the destructive X-basis measurements (MRX) of the 15 tetrahedral-code qubits, in the code-qubit ordering', matching the problem statement and solution.

issues.description: In the template, `simulate_msd_one_round` constructs a circuit using `stim.Circuit(n_shots)`, but `stim.Circuit` does not take a shot count argument (shots are provided to `sampler.sample(n_shots)`). This makes the starter code fail immediately at runtime even before students implement the function body.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template to construct circuits with `stim.Circuit()` (no arguments). Keep `n_shots` only when calling `sim.sample(n_shots)`.

issues.description: The `inject` function's parameter typing is inconsistent: the problem statement lists `inject(circ: stim.Circuit, data_qubit: int, injection_qubit) -> int` (no type annotation for `injection_qubit`), while the template docstring specifies `injection_qubit (int)` and the solution uses it as an integer qubit index. This can confuse students (and any type-checking/autograding that expects the annotated signature).
issues.suggestedFix: Update the problem statement signature to `inject(circ: stim.Circuit, data_qubit: int, injection_qubit: int) -> int` to match the template/solution usage.
